Familial melanoma primarily arises in skin; pancreatic and other cancers are separate diseases, and ocular disease is a minority subtype.

Autoinflammatory sterile abscesses predominantly affect spleen (~70%); hepatic abscesses are frequent (30–79%). Skin involvement is less consistent despite the skin-disorder parent.

Inherited porokeratosis is a cutaneous keratinization disorder; the MVD gene alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Carcinoma in situ originates in breast ducts; breast has no axis.

Inflammation of the conjunctiva; the umbrella includes infectious, allergic and irritant causes, so no single immune mechanism applies throughout.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 7/7, developmental delay in 4/4 and brain atrophy in 2/2. Optic atrophy in 1/7 is below threshold.
Progressive destructive joint disease; the underlying neuropathy is a separate causative disorder rather than nerve damage produced by the arthropathy.
Most malignant germ cell tumors arise in reproductive organs, which have no axis; extragonadal subtypes do not establish a shared covered organ across the umbrella.
Chronic inflammation of the lacrimal gland; an autoimmune or infectious cause is not specified.
Infiltrative fibroblastic neoplasm of soft connective tissues, commonly fascia and musculoaponeurotic structures.
Magnesium depletion is a mineral/electrolyte disorder; cramps, weakness and paresthesias do not establish common direct muscle or nerve damage.
Bacterial infections characteristically targeting blood cells, including granulocytes and monocytes; no additional organ damage is shared commonly across the group.
Bartonella infection umbrella; hemolysis, vascular lesions and endocarditis characterize particular forms rather than most patients across the group.
Autoimmune Guillain-Barre variant directly affecting peripheral sensory nerves.
Skeletal dysplasia and cataracts define CLSD; dental hypoplasia/tooth loss occur in 80–99%, caries in 14/14, and sparse/brittle hair in 4/4.
Focal neurologic dystonia defined by impaired laryngeal muscle control and voice function; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Cystine transport/storage disorder confined clinically to cornea and conjunctiva, with visual impairment; definition explicitly excludes systemic manifestations.
Defined by progressive sensorineural deafness, alopecia and hypogonadism with LH/GH deficiencies.
Disorders of hair follicles and associated sebaceous glands; additional organs and mechanisms depend on subtype.
Disease of a single peripheral nerve in the upper limb; no specific autoimmune or infectious cause is established.
IgE-mediated hypersensitivity defines the disease; skin, airway, eye and gastrointestinal involvement vary by subtype without shared common direct organ damage.
